label: Contender, Then Champion
line: Ask a superlative question, score a plausible candidate out loud, then bring in the winner nobody guessed and count past the candidate.
best_for: a superlative with a countable measure and a winner that is not the obvious one
also_for: two things compared on one measure, when the expected one loses
avoid_for: a superlative whose winner everyone knows
a measure that cannot be counted
a ranking of many items: use a ladder
signals: the real winner is not the obvious one

beats.name: Question
beats.job: The superlative, asked in one sentence.

beats.name: The contender, scored
beats.job: Item by item, to a total.

beats.name: Turn
beats.job: One line: that is still not the most.

beats.name: The champion's case
beats.job: What counts against it first, then its tally, passing the contender.

beats.name: Final score
beats.job: The number, and that it is the most.

hooks.shape: Which [thing] has the most [measure]? [Plausible contender] is a contender.
[Contender] has [N] [measure]. That is not the record.
The [thing] with the most [measure] is not [the one you would guess].

holds: The contender's score gives the viewer a number to beat, and it stays in view while the champion's tally climbs past it.
ending: The final score. Nothing after it.
pitfalls: Facts in date order with no contender
Naming the champion before scoring the contender
A tally the viewer cannot follow item by item
template: Which [thing] has the most [measure]? You would guess [candidate]: [tally], which makes [N]. But that is still not the most. Despite [handicap], [winner]: [tally, with one complication]. That makes [M], the most in the world.
